precepts.text: Moreover Manasseh shed innocent blood very much, till he had filled Jerusalem from one end to another. He was behind a lot of death, sorcery, and witchcraft; and the Lord forgave Manasseh when he humbled himself in affliction, and put him back on the throne. The Lord has mercy on whom he will have mercy. That is why it is very important for us to learn humility: people fall, and the Most High is able to raise them up again, like David. But do not abuse it. You are not David; you are not Manasseh; you are not Moses. The Lord puts it there to remind us that his graces and mercies were around back then too. Do not get prideful. Humility.
precepts.point: After this he took away the strange gods and the idol out of the house of the Lord, cast them out of the city, repaired the altar of the Lord, and commanded Judah to serve the Lord God of Israel.

note.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time

precepts.why:
Kings tells the same account in its own way. It had already said Manasseh “hath done wickedly above all that the Amorites did, which were before him, and hath made Judah also to sin with his idols.” He went above the Amorites; Manasseh was a monster. Chronicles gives more of the detail: he “caused his children to pass through the fire”, ancient abortions, burning his babies alive; he observed times, used enchantments and witchcraft, dealt with a familiar spirit and with wizards; he was a sorcerer. And he put an idol in the temple.

Then Kings adds what Chronicles leaves out: “Moreover Manasseh shed innocent blood very much, till he had filled Jerusalem from one end to another.” Babies on babies. That is a lot of blood, from one end of Jerusalem to the other. And it was not only him: the people did the same thing, for this was “beside his sin wherewith he made Judah to sin, in doing that which was evil in the sight of the Lord.”

Manasseh was behind a lot of death, sorcery and witchcraft; he did evil way beyond worthy of death. He killed babies, he went into witchcraft, he defiled the temple. And yet, when he was in affliction and humbled himself greatly, the Lord forgave Manasseh, heard his supplication, and put him back on the throne. The Lord has mercy on whom he will have mercy.

That is why it is so important for us to learn humility. People fall, and the Most High is able to raise them up again, like David. But don't abuse it. All of us in here ain't David; don't think, I can do what David did. No, negro, you ain't David. You're not Manasseh. You ain't Moses. The Lord puts it there to remind us that the graces and mercies of Christ were around back then too, from time to time. Don't get stupid and get prideful. Humility.

precepts.text: The Most High will take away the hedge of His vineyard, lay it waste, and command the clouds to rain no rain, the same desolation promised over Jerusalem.
precepts.point: He will forsake the remnant of His inheritance and deliver them into the hand of their enemies to be a prey and a spoil, because they have provoked Him to anger since the day their fathers came out of Egypt. The Most High has borne with this wickedness for hundreds of years.

note.label: 2 Kings 21: The Wickedness of Manasseh and Amon

precepts.why:
“I will take away the hedge thereof, and it shall be eaten up; and break down the wall thereof, and it shall be trodden down: And I will lay it waste”, and “I will also command the clouds that they rain no rain upon it.”

Israel is his vineyard, and this is the same desolation promised over Jerusalem for Manasseh’s wickedness: “I will stretch over Jerusalem the line of Samaria, and the plummet of the house of Ahab: and I will wipe Jerusalem as a man wipeth a dish, wiping it, and turning it upside down.” What was done to Samaria reaches Judah. The hedge comes down, and the remnant of his inheritance becomes “a prey and a spoil to all their enemies.”

precepts.text: The people are destroyed for lack of knowledge, and because they rejected the knowledge of the law, the Most High rejects them.
precepts.point: He will forsake the remnant of His inheritance and deliver them into the hand of their enemies to be a prey and a spoil, because they have provoked Him to anger since the day their fathers came out of Egypt. The Most High has borne with this wickedness for hundreds of years.

note.label: 2 Kings 21: The Wickedness of Manasseh and Amon

precepts.why:
“My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge: because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee”, “seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God, I will also forget thy children.”

Because Judah rejected the knowledge of the law, the Most High rejects them: “I will forsake the remnant of mine inheritance, and deliver them into the hand of their enemies.” They have provoked him to anger “since the day their fathers came forth out of Egypt, even unto this day.” He bore with this wickedness for hundreds of years, and now it is rejection for rejection.

precepts.text: The people are gone into captivity for having no knowledge, and hell, meaning captivity, has enlarged herself and opened her mouth without measure.
precepts.point: He will forsake the remnant of His inheritance and deliver them into the hand of their enemies to be a prey and a spoil, because they have provoked Him to anger since the day their fathers came out of Egypt. The Most High has borne with this wickedness for hundreds of years.

note.label: 2 Kings 21: The Wickedness of Manasseh and Amon

precepts.why:
“Therefore my people are gone into captivity, because they have no knowledge: and their honourable men are famished, and their multitude dried up with thirst. Therefore hell hath enlarged herself, and opened her mouth without measure.”

Hell here means captivity. Having no knowledge, the people go into captivity, and it opens its mouth without measure: “their glory, and their multitude, and their pomp, and he that rejoiceth, shall descend into it.”

That is the evil the Most High brought on Jerusalem and Judah, such that “whosoever heareth of it, both his ears shall tingle”: the remnant of his inheritance delivered into the hand of their enemies.

precepts.text: The captains of the king of Assyria take Manasseh among the thorns and carry him bound to Babylon, then held by Assyria.
precepts.point: The history shows a power struggle beginning, where Assyrian kings ruled over Babylon, and later Babylonian kings ruled over Assyria; Manasseh sleeps with his fathers and Amon his son reigns.

note.label: 2 Kings 21: The Wickedness of Manasseh and Amon

precepts.why:
“Wherefore the Lord brought upon them the captains of the host of the king of Assyria, which took Manasseh among the thorns, and bound him with fetters, and carried him to Babylon.”

The rest of the acts of Manasseh are written in the chronicles, and this is part of what Kings leaves out. The captains of the king of Assyria carried him bound to Babylon, which was then a province under Assyria. There he repented and prayed, and the prayer of Manasseh is recorded in the Apocrypha, prayed while he was held captive in Babylon.

It also shows the power struggle beginning, with Assyrian kings ruling over Babylon.

precepts.text: Nebuchadnezzar, a Babylonian, reigns over the Assyrians in Nineveh, showing Babylon rising to take all that Assyria held.
precepts.point: The history shows a power struggle beginning, where Assyrian kings ruled over Babylon, and later Babylonian kings ruled over Assyria; Manasseh sleeps with his fathers and Amon his son reigns.

note.label: 2 Kings 21: The Wickedness of Manasseh and Amon

precepts.why:
“In the twelfth year of the reign of Nabuchodonosor, who reigned in Nineve, the great city.”

Nebuchadnezzar, a Babylonian, reigns over the Assyrians in Nineveh. In Manasseh’s day the captains of the king of Assyria carried him to Babylon, then a province under Assyria. Later the order is turned: Babylonian kings rule over Assyria. Babylon is rising to take all that Assyria held.

points: Manasseh king of Judah seduced them to do more evil than did the nations whom the Lord destroyed before the children of Israel. He did wickedly above all that the Amorites did, and made Judah also to sin with his idols. The Amorites were terrible; Manasseh went above them.

note.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time

points: Manasseh did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, after the abominations of the heathen. He built up again the high places which Hezekiah his father had destroyed, reared up altars for Baal, worshiped all the host of heaven, built altars in the house of the Lord, made his son pass through the fire, observed times, used enchantments, and dealt with familiar spirits and wizards. He went back and served the same gods and altars his father destroyed.

note.label: In Vain Do They Worship Me! Religious Syncretism

points: The Lord said Israel would not be moved out of the land, only if they would observe to do according to all that Moses commanded. But they hearkened not: and Manasseh seduced them to do more evil than did the nations whom the Lord destroyed before the children of Israel. We went crazier than the heathen.

note.label: In Vain Do They Worship Me! Religious Syncretism

points: Manasseh began at twelve and reigned fifty-five years, and did not follow his father's example: he rebuilt the high places Hezekiah had cast down, reared altars to Baal and a grove as Ahab did, and worshipped the host of heaven, the stars and the zodiac.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

points: He built altars for the host of heaven in the two courts of the temple where the Lord had put his name, and made his son pass through the fire. He became another Solomon, but far worse.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

points: Observing times, enchantments, familiar spirits and wizards: witchcraft and sorcery. He seduced Judah to do more evil than the nations the Lord destroyed before Israel, a wicked king and a bad influencer.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

points: Because of Manasseh the Lord promised evil on Jerusalem to make both ears tingle, the line of Samaria and the plummet of the house of Ahab: the same judgment that sent Assyria against the northern kingdom would now fall on Judah.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

points: Wiping Jerusalem as a man wipes a dish and turns it upside down is deportation out of the land. The innocent blood from one end of Jerusalem to the other was the children sacrificed under his edict, the ancient abortions.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

points: Manasseh begins to reign at twelve years old and reigns fifty-five years, doing evil after the abominations of the heathen the Most High cast out before Israel.

note.label: 2 Kings 21: The Wickedness of Manasseh and Amon

note.label: 2 Kings 21: The Wickedness of Manasseh and Amon

points: He makes his son pass through the fire, observes times, uses enchantments, and deals with familiar spirits and wizards, provoking the Most High to anger, and seduces Judah to do more evil than the nations the Most High destroyed.

note.label: 2 Kings 21: The Wickedness of Manasseh and Amon

points: The Most High speaks by His servants the prophets that because Manasseh did wickedly above all the Amorites and made Judah to sin, He is bringing such evil upon Jerusalem that both ears of whoever hears it shall tingle.

note.label: 2 Kings 21: The Wickedness of Manasseh and Amon

note.label: 2 Kings 21: The Wickedness of Manasseh and Amon

points: Amon begins to reign at twenty-two years old and reigns two years, doing evil as his father Manasseh did, walking in all his ways and serving the idols his father served.

note.label: 2 Kings 21: The Wickedness of Manasseh and Amon

points: He forsakes the Most High God of his fathers and walks not in His way.

note.label: 2 Kings 21: The Wickedness of Manasseh and Amon
